title: Office Ping user manual
intro: Office Ping is a digital tap on the shoulder. Instead of walking over or calling, you send a short message (a **ping**) that pops up on the other person's screen. They click **Acknowledge** so you know they've seen it.

steps: Open **https://ping.tejgyan.org** in Chrome or Edge.
Sign in with the username and password your admin gave you. There is no sign-up page: an admin creates every account.
When the banner at the top of the page asks, click **Enable**, then **Allow** in the browser's pop-up. This lets pings show as desktop notifications.
Change the password your admin gave you (see *Your password*).

blocks.tip: **Want a quick walkthrough?** Click **Show me around** at the top of the Help page for a one-minute guided tour of the real screens. Sections below also have short animated demos.

blocks.p: **Finding your way around.** On a computer, every page is in the dark sidebar on the left; HR and admins find Groups, Templates and the admin pages under **Manage** (click it to open). On a phone or tablet, the main pages (Overview, People, Inbox, Messages) are in the bar at the bottom of the screen, and everything else, including History, your status, Help, Change password and Sign out, is under **More**.

blocks.tip: **Keep Office Ping open.** You only receive alerts while an Office Ping window or tab is open somewhere. Minimised or in the background is fine. If it's closed, pings wait in your Inbox until you open it again. Easiest: make it open by itself when your computer starts (see *Open Office Ping automatically at start-up*).

sections.title: Open Office Ping automatically at start-up

blocks.p: You only get pings while Office Ping is open. Set it up once and it opens by itself, in its own window, every time you start or restart your computer. It takes a minute, needs no administrator rights, and works with Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge.

steps: Click **Download the Windows setup file** below.
Open your **Downloads** folder, right-click **office-ping-windows.ps1** and choose **Run with PowerShell**. If Windows asks whether to run it, choose **Open** or **Run anyway**.
Office Ping opens. From now on it opens by itself (minimised, on the taskbar) each time you sign in.

Paste this line and press **Enter**:

blocks.p: Office Ping opens, and it's also in your app menu as **Office Ping**.

blocks.tip: **Minimise, don't close.** Keep the Office Ping window open in the background. If you close it, you won't get pings until you open it again (or restart your computer).

**Mac:** run the same line with *--remove* at the end, as below.
**Linux:** run the same line with *--remove* at the end, as below.

blocks.p: **From the Overview page** (the first page after signing in):

steps: Start typing a name, team or email in the search box and pick the person.
Click one of the quick templates (for example *Please come to my desk*), or type your own message (up to 500 characters). HR and admins choose which three appear here.
Tick **Mark urgent** only if it really can't wait.
Click **Send ping**.

blocks.p: **On a phone**, the Overview is one screen with everything you need:

list: **Tap a face** in the row under the search box to choose that person (it gets a gold ring), or type a name in the search box. HR and admins can switch the search box between **Person** and **Group**.
**Tap one of the three quick messages** to fill in the message box, or type your own.
Tap **Send**. It stays just above the keyboard while you type.
**To nudge**, press and hold a face, or tap **Nudge** with the message box empty.

blocks.p: **From the People page:** you see everyone, with who's online right now at the top.

list: **Ping** opens a small window with the quick templates. Press **Ctrl + Enter** to send.
**Nudge** sends "👋 Nudge" straight away, with no window: a quick tap on the shoulder. **Ping** lets you write a message.
The **Recent** row on the Overview page lists people you pinged lately, with the same Nudge and Ping buttons.

blocks.p: **From any page:** press **Ctrl + K** (**⌘ K** on a Mac), or **/** when you're not typing in a box, or click **Quick ping** at the top of the sidebar. Type a name, pick a template and send without leaving the page you're on.

blocks.tip: **Check their status first.** If someone has set a status such as *In a meeting* or *Do not disturb*, you'll see it next to their name and in the message window. A normal ping then waits quietly in their inbox; mark it urgent only if it really can't wait.

blocks.p: You can see whether they received and acknowledged it on the **History** page.

blocks.tip: **Urgent** pings appear in red and jump ahead of any other pings waiting for that person. Keep urgent for real emergencies so people keep taking it seriously.

blocks.p: To prevent spamming, everyone can send up to **5 pings a minute**. A ping to a whole group counts as one. If you go over, Office Ping tells you how many seconds to wait.

So that nobody gets bombarded, you can ping the **same person at most twice a minute**, and you can't send them the **same message twice** within a minute. If they haven't answered, give them a moment, or walk over.
When someone pings you, the page dims and a pop-up appears in the middle of the screen showing who sent it, when, and the message. At the same time:

list: A short chime plays (three notes for urgent pings).
A desktop notification appears and **stays until you click it**, even if you're working in another program. Clicking it brings Office Ping to the front.
The browser tab title flashes **🔔 Sender's name** until you deal with the ping.

blocks.p: In the pop-up, tap a quick reply or choose a button:

head: Button
What it does
rows: **On my way**, **Coming in 2 min**, **In a meeting**, **Can't right now**
Acknowledges the ping and sends that reply. The sender sees it straight away.
**Acknowledge**
Tells the sender you've got it, without a reply. The ping is done.
**Later**
Closes the pop-up. The ping stays unacknowledged in your Inbox. Pressing **Esc** does the same.

blocks.p: **Urgent pings come back.** If you haven't acknowledged an urgent ping after 5 minutes, it pops up again marked *Reminder*, and the sender is told you haven't answered yet.
**In a meeting or Do not disturb?** Normal pings then skip the pop-up and the sound and wait in your Inbox. Urgent pings still pop up. See *Your status*.
If several pings arrive, they're shown one at a time. Click **N more waiting · Open inbox** to see them all at once.

blocks.tip: Signed in on two computers, or in two tabs? Each one shows the ping, but once you acknowledge it on one, it disappears from the others.

blocks.p: **Messages** is a quiet one-to-one chat for things that don't need an answer this minute. Unlike a ping, a message never pops up in the middle of the screen or plays a sound: you get a red number on **Messages**, and a desktop notification if Office Ping is in the background.

steps: On the **People** page, click **Message** next to the person. Or open **Messages**, click **New message** and pick them.
Type your message. On a computer, press **Enter** to send (**Shift + Enter** starts a new line). On a phone, tap the send button.
**Seen** appears under your last message once they've read it, and you see *typing…* while they write back.

blocks.p: On a computer, your chats are also in the **Messages** bar in the bottom-right corner of every page. Click it to see them, and click a chat to open it in a small window while you carry on working.
Click **Ping** at the top of a chat to send that person a ping instead. It pops up on their screen until they acknowledge it.

list: You get a desktop notification for a new message only when that chat isn't already open in front of you.
While your status is **In a meeting** or **Do not disturb**, messages arrive silently, with no notification.
To silence one chat, click the bell next to **Ping** (*Mute this chat*). The red number still shows.

blocks.tip: **Who can read my chats?** In Office Ping, only you and the other person. The audit log records that a chat was started, never what was said. Chat is a work tool, so write as you would in any work message.

sections.title: Your status: meeting, lunch, do not disturb

blocks.p: Let people know you're busy before they ping you.

steps: On a computer, click the line above your name at the bottom of the sidebar (it says *Available · set a status*). On a phone, tap **More**, then **Set status**.
Choose **In a meeting**, **Do not disturb**, **Out for lunch** or **Away from desk**, and add a note if you like (for example *Board review*).
Choose when it should clear: 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, end of day, a time you pick, or until you clear it.
Click **Set status**.

head: Status
What happens to pings
rows: **In a meeting**, **Do not disturb**
Normal pings wait quietly in your Inbox: no pop-up, no sound. Urgent pings still pop up.
**Out for lunch**, **Away from desk**
Pings arrive as usual. People see your status before they ping you.

blocks.p: While a status is on, a bar at the top of every page reminds you. Click **I'm back** to clear it early. Your status shows next to your name on People, in the Recent list and when someone picks you to ping.
The Inbox lists every ping sent to you. The number next to **Inbox** (in the sidebar, or on the bottom bar on a phone) is how many you haven't read.

list: **Urgent, waiting for you** at the top lists urgent pings you haven't acknowledged yet.
The same message sent several times in a row (for example *👋 Nudge ×8*) shows as one row; **Acknowledge all** handles them together.
**Reply** shows the quick replies; **Acknowledge** answers without one.
**All / Unread** switches between everything and only unread pings. **Show more** loads older ones.
**Mark all read** clears the unread count. It does **not** acknowledge the pings: senders still see them as not acknowledged.

blocks.p: **History** shows pings you sent (**My sent**) and pings you received (**My received**), with their status:

head: Status
Meaning
rows: **Sent**
Not on their screen yet: they're offline or Office Ping isn't open. They'll get it when they open it (within 24 hours), and it's always in their Inbox.
**Delivered**
It reached their screen, but they haven't acknowledged it yet.
**Acknowledged**
They clicked Acknowledge.

blocks.p: Pings to a group show progress such as **2/3 delivered · 1 ack**.
Under each ping you also see any quick reply, such as *↩ “On my way”*.

**Finding a ping.** Use the search box (message text or a name), **Anyone** to pick a person, the status list (for example *Awaiting ack*), **From / to** dates and **Urgent only**. **Clear filters** resets them. The filters stay in the page address, so you can bookmark a view.

steps: On a computer, click the **key icon** at the bottom of the sidebar. On a phone, tap **More → Change password**.
Enter your current password, then your new password twice.
Click **Change password**. Use the new password next time you sign in.

blocks.p: Passwords need at least 8 characters and can't be a common password, only numbers, or too close to your name.
**Forgot your password?** Ask an admin to reset it. They'll give you a temporary password; change it straight away under **Change password**.

head: Problem
What to do
rows: I don't get pop-ups or notifications

Make sure an Office Ping tab is open, and that your status isn't *In a meeting* or *Do not disturb* (those keep normal pings quiet). Check notifications are allowed: click the lock icon left of the address → **Notifications → Allow**. Turn off Windows *Focus assist* / *Do not disturb* (or macOS *Focus*).
I hear no sound
Check your computer's volume and that the browser tab isn't muted (right-click the tab).
I show as offline
You're shown online while Office Ping is open. It updates within a minute.
I can't sign in
Check Caps Lock. If you've forgotten your password, ask an admin to reset it.
"Too many failed sign-ins. Try again in …"
After 5 wrong passwords, sign-in for that username pauses for 15 minutes. Wait, or ask an admin to reset your password.
"This site can't be reached"
Check your internet connection and try again in a few minutes. If it continues, tell IT.
"You can send 5 pings a minute" when sending
You've reached the limit. Wait the number of seconds shown, then send again.
"You've already pinged … twice" or "You just sent … this same message"
You can ping one person twice a minute, and not with the same message. Wait the number of seconds shown.

blocks.p: HR and admins see live numbers next to the message box on the Overview page (on a phone, at the top of **History**, under **More**). Click any card to open the matching list.

head: Card
Counts
rows: **Teammates**, **Online now**, **Offline**
Active accounts other than you, the same people as on the People page.
**Pings today**
Every ping sent by anyone since midnight. Opens History filtered to today.
**Awaiting ack**
Pings from the last 24 hours that haven't been acknowledged. Opens History with the *Awaiting ack* filter.

blocks.p: **Recent pings** below shows the latest activity across the office, with urgent pings nobody has acknowledged at the top. HR and admins can also choose **All** on the History page to see everyone's pings.

HR and admins can ping a whole team at once: on the Overview page, click **A group**, pick the group, write the message and click **Send ping**. Every member gets it, and History shows how many received and acknowledged it.
On the **Groups** page:

list: **Create a new group:** enter a name (for example *Backend Team*) and an optional description, then click **Create**.
**Add a member:** choose a person from **+ Add member…** under the group.
**Remove a member:** click the **×** next to their name.
**Delete** removes the whole group. Past pings stay in History.

blocks.p: A group ping counts as **one** ping toward the limit of 5 a minute, however many members the group has.
Templates are the ready-made messages everyone sees as one-click buttons when sending a ping.

list: On the **Templates** page, enter a short title and the message, then click **Add**.
Turn on **Home screen** for up to **3** templates. Those are the quick buttons on everyone's Overview, on computers and phones. Until you choose, the first three are shown.
Every template is still available in **Quick ping** (Ctrl + K) and in the window that opens from **Ping** on the People page.
Click **Delete** to remove one; that also frees its home-screen place.
Keep the titles short (a few words), so the buttons stay easy to read.

blocks.p: Go to **Admin → Users**.

steps: Under **Create a new user**, fill in username, email, a starting password (8+ characters), name, department and role.
Click **Create user**, then give the person their username and starting password privately.
Ask them to change the password under **Change password** after their first sign-in.

head: Role
Can do
rows: **Member**
Send and receive pings to people, Inbox, own History, change own password.
Everything a member can, plus ping groups, manage groups and templates, see **All** history.
**Admin**
Everything HR can, plus manage users, reset passwords and view the audit log.

list: **Change a role** with the dropdown in the user's row.
**Deactivate** blocks someone from signing in (for example when they leave). Their history is kept. **Activate** lets them back in.
Your own row shows **Change my password** instead, so you can't lock yourself out by accident.

steps: On **Admin → Users**, click **Reset password** in the person's row.
A strong, easy-to-read password is suggested (for example *Kp7m-Qx4z-Rt9w*). Click **Generate** for another, or type your own.
Click **Copy**, then **Reset password**.
Give the new password to the person privately (in person or by phone, not in a group chat), and ask them to change it under **Change password**.

blocks.p: The old password stops working immediately, and the reset is recorded in the audit log (the password itself is never stored there).

blocks.tip: A reset doesn't sign the person out of devices where they're already signed in; those sessions end on their own within 7 days. If you suspect someone else is using the account, deactivate it first.

blocks.p: **Admin → Audit log** (under **Manage**) records who did what and from which IP address: sign-ins and failed sign-ins, sign-outs, password changes and resets, user, group and template changes, every ping sent and acknowledged (with any quick reply), urgent pings that had to be re-sent (**PING_ESCALATED**) and history exports (**PINGS_EXPORTED**).
Use the search box to filter by action (for example *PASSWORD_RESET*), person, target or IP address.

**PING_BLOCKED** means someone tried to ping the same person too often, or repeat the same message. It's logged at most once a minute per pair. Several of these from one person towards the same colleague can be a sign of pestering worth a quiet word.

**LOGIN_FAILED** entries are worth a look: several for one username can mean someone is guessing a password. After 5 failures the username is locked for 15 minutes, and after 20 failures from one IP address that address is locked too.

steps: Open **History**, choose **All**, and set any filters (person, dates, status, urgent).
Click **Export CSV**. A spreadsheet of every matching ping downloads, with sender, recipient, message, status and acknowledgement times.

blocks.p: Each export is recorded in the audit log. The file contains people's messages, so store and share it carefully.

list: Keep at least two admin accounts, so one admin can reset the other.
Deactivate accounts on the day someone leaves.
Look through the audit log now and then for password resets or user changes you don't recognise.
Use your own account for daily pinging and keep admin work to admin tasks.
